sources.title: Hamilton Microlab VANTAGE product page
sources.notes: Provides the official 1.3 m and 2.0 m system dimensions, deck capacities, sample-loading wording, and confirms 360-degree device integration around the platform.

sources.title: Hamilton Microlab VANTAGE site requirements PDF
sources.notes: Provides shipping-crate footprints and configuration weights for the 1.3 m and 2.0 m pipettor, logistics cabinet, rear integration cabinet, and track gripper.

sources.title: Hamilton official Microlab VANTAGE 1.3 front-closed render
sources.notes: Primary visual reference for the stacked upper pipetting enclosure, lower logistics cabinet glazing, dual front handle bars, and central pipetting head silhouette.

sources.title: Hamilton official Microlab VANTAGE 2.0 front-closed render
sources.notes: Used to verify that the 2.0 m system preserves the same stacked front silhouette while extending the deck width and status-light span.

sources.title: Hamilton official Optional Track Gripper exploded render
sources.notes: Used to estimate the open-top deck depth, the lower logistics-cabinet volume, and the right-side handoff / under-deck access region.

collision_model.notes: The simplified collision intentionally removes the single full-body envelope. The upper deck remains reachable from above and from the front, while the lower loading tray is modeled as a separate fixed, extended collision outside the body shell.

access_points.name: deck_access_link
access_points.description: Approximate center of the primary pipetting deck / work surface inside the upper enclosure.
access_points.collision_notes: This access frame is intentionally positioned over the collision-free main work surface so vertical approach and front approach onto the deck remain valid.

access_points.name: front_loading_access_link
access_points.description: Approximate robot-facing access point immediately outside the upper front enclosure where manual front service or front-facing loading interactions would occur.
access_points.collision_notes: This access face sits in front of the open front cutout of the upper enclosure rather than inside the segmented shell collision.

access_points.name: loading_tray_access_link
access_points.description: Estimated right-front handoff point for the lower Entry/Exit / autoload region visible in official front and exploded renders.
access_points.collision_notes: This access frame is tray-backed by the fixed, extended lower loading tray and is intentionally kept outside the body-shell collision volumes.

access_points.name: front_service_access_link
access_points.description: Approximate center of the upper front service face aligned with the dual handle bars and service window.
access_points.collision_notes: This service face is aligned to the segmented front opening and remains forward of the upper shell collision.

access_points.name: logistics_cabinet_access_link
access_points.description: Approximate center of the lower logistics-cabinet front glazing used for under-deck consumable access.
access_points.collision_notes: This lower-front access face is kept in the front glazing cutout zone so it is not embedded in the lower body shell collision.

access_points.name: rear_service_access_link
access_points.description: Approximate rear utility and maintenance region for cables, services, and rear-side integrations.
access_points.collision_notes: This rear service frame is placed behind the shortened rear shell collision so back-side utility access remains reachable.

access_points.name: socketTypeGenericSbsFootprint_1_60_1
access_points.description: Representative SBS work reference on the exposed upper pipetting deck.
access_points.collision_notes: This SBS work reference stays on the collision-free upper deck opening and is not embedded in the segmented shell.

access_points.name: socketTypeGenericSbsFootprint_2_60_1
access_points.description: Representative SBS handoff reference on the fixed, extended lower loading tray.
access_points.collision_notes: This SBS handoff reference is anchored to the tray-backed loading region rather than the body shell, keeping the loading zone reachable.

notes: No public Hamilton CAD, STL, STEP, OBJ, GLB, or similar directly reusable 3D model was located during web search on official public pages, so this package remains a fallback representation rather than an OEM mesh import.

The mesh is now a segmented official-image-guided proxy instead of a single envelope box: it distinguishes the upper pipetting enclosure, lower logistics cabinet, glazing, front handle bars, deck surface, and approximate internal handoff structures.

Access points are integration-oriented estimates derived from official front renders, product-page wording about sample loading and 360-degree device integration, and the exploded track-gripper render; they should not be treated as factory metrology.
